model_answer: Rein calls one function for a reply, and the rest of the code never asks which model is behind it. A scripted model answers from a fixed list, so every run repeats exactly, and no key is needed. A real model makes the same call and returns the same kind of reply. I keep the raw content blocks, because a tool request can come after text. Then the loop reads the stop reason and the blocks, not just the first one.
prompt: Show me the one interface your code calls for a reply. What changes when the model is scripted?
rubric: Names one model interface that both implementations sit behind
Says a scripted model repeats exactly and needs no key
Notes that the reply's content is a list of blocks, so the first block is not always the tool request
Names stop_reason as the field that says why the model stopped

model_answer: The API is stateless. Each request carries only the messages I send in it, so a second run knows nothing about the first unless its request includes those messages. To make a run remember, the harness has to send the history with every call. That costs input tokens, because the whole history is sent again each time.
prompt: Three runs of one script never remember each other. Why, and what would change that?
rubric: Says the API is stateless and each request carries only what it sends
Says a run remembers only if its request includes the earlier messages
Mentions that resending the history costs input tokens
Says each run is a new request, not a continued session
